terms.document: Sports Reference LLC — Web Site Terms of Use (Last Updated: May 19, 2023)
terms.quote: 5. Permitted Use — "In addition to the terms below, please see our data use and licensing guidelines and our Bot Traffic/Limiting page for some specific discussion and guidance. SRL believes in data democratization—open access to data and the tools that use it. Yes, we charge for some tools, but we strive to keep prices affordable for most users and to provide access to others, including underrepresented communities. Moreover, we encourage the sharing and reuse of data and statistics our users find on our Site as a general matter, but our business obviously would be harmed if a bad apple were to abuse that privilege to create a competing statistical database or to copy a materially significant portion of our data. So, to strike an appropriate balance between these goals, and to protect our business, our technology infrastructure, and our ability to continue to provide interesting and robust sports statistics to our users, this section of our Agreement sets forth certain restrictions on permitted uses of this Site and its Content. Our guiding principles are that (1) sharing, using, modifying, repackaging, or publishing data found on individual SRL webpages is welcomed, whether for commercial or non-commercial purposes, but (2) any such sharing, use, modification, repackaging, or publication should explicitly credit SRL as the source of the data to the maximum extent possible and (3) any such sharing, use, modification, repackaging, or publication must not violate any express restrictions set forth in this Section 5, especially the restrictions set forth in subparts 5(i) and 5(j) below." | Enumerated prohibitions: "Subject to the terms of this Agreement, you are granted a limited, personal, non-exclusive, non-sublicensable, non-assignable, non-transferable, and revocable license to access and use the Site and Content. However, except as expressly permitted by this Agreement, in connection with the use of the Site, you may not: ... without our express written permission, use any automated means to access or use the Site, including scripts, bots, scrapers, data miners, or similar software, in a manner that adversely impacts site performance or access; or use any material or Content from the Site, including without limitation any statistics or data, (i) to create any database, archive, or other data store that competes with or constitutes a material substitute for the services or data stores offered on the Site or by the Site's Data Providers or (ii) to provide any service that competes with or constitutes a material substitute for the services or data stores offered on the Site or by the Site's Data Providers; or copy or use any material or Content from the Site, including without limitation any statistics, data, text, graphics, or images, for purposes of training, fine-tuning, prompting, or instructing artificial intelligence models or technologies in any manner, including without limitation for purposes of (i) generating answers, text, scores, statistics, notes, graphics, images, or any other output; or (ii) supporting machine learning methods used to predict, classify, label, or score inputs into the models; or ..." | 2. Proprietary Rights — "SRL owns or licenses the data, statistics, text, graphics, images, forms, artwork, sound recordings, audio, video, software, and other material for this Site (the "Content"), as well as the selection, coordination, arrangement, and organization and enhancement of the Content (also, the "Content") for this Site." | 6. Teachers and Search Engines — "Notwithstanding any other terms of this Agreement, SRL grants the right to teachers to print pages from the Site for distribution to students, provided that proper attribution is given to the URL on the Site where the material originated. Notwithstanding any other terms of this Agreement, SRL also grant the operators of search engines permission to use robots to copy materials and Content from the site for the sole purpose of creating publicly available searchable indexes of the materials, but not caches, copies, or archives of the materials or Content for any other non-indexing purpose. Search engines are expected to follow the guidelines set forth in the robots.txt file that we provide." | 21. "This Agreement will be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania... You agree that you will not bring or be a party to any class-action lawsuit against SRL."
terms.basis: Character-for-character from the fetched page; the only alteration is collapsing the HTML's hard line-wrapping to single spaces, and the clause list is quoted in the document's own order with the intervening bullets I did not need marked by ellipsis. (a) CITE ONE FACT rests on guiding principle (1): "sharing, using, modifying, repackaging, or publishing data found on individual SRL webpages is welcomed, whether for commercial or non-commercial purposes" — the broadest permission any holder on this list grants, and it is explicit that COMMERCIAL use is included. It is conditioned by (2), "should explicitly credit SRL as the source of the data to the maximum extent possible" — which the project already satisfies with a link back on every card. (b) EXTRACT FACTS is restricted, not permitted, on two clauses pulling in opposite directions. Principle (1) covers "repackaging" data from individual pages, which is exactly what hand extraction into an own database is, and the effective date of that language is May 19, 2023. But two later subparts bite: the automated-means clause forbids "scripts, bots, scrapers, data miners, or similar software" "without our express written permission" — note the qualifier "in a manner that adversely impacts site performance or access", which is what makes this restricted rather than flatly prohibited: a slow, rate-respecting fetch is arguably outside the clause, a fast one is squarely inside it. The second bite is harder and directly aimed at how this project works: the AI clause bars copying Content "for purposes of training, fine-tuning, PROMPTING, or INSTRUCTING artificial intelligence models or technologies in any manner, including without limitation for purposes of (i) generating answers, text, scores, statistics...". Pasting a b-ref page into a model to have it write or check a card is prompting an AI model with their Content to generate answers and statistics. On the document's own words that is prohibited, and it is prohibited whether a human or a script did the fetching. (c) AGGREGATE AT SCALE is prohibited outright by the material-substitute clause: "(i) to create any database, archive, or other data store that competes with or constitutes a material substitute for the services or data stores offered on the Site". The preamble names the concern in plain English — "a bad apple" abusing the privilege "to create a competing statistical database or to copy a materially significant portion of our data". Note what the clause is NOT: it is a competition/substitution test, not a volume test. A trivia bank of a few thousand discrete facts with links back is not a substitute for basketball-reference.com; a mirror of their season tables is. That distinction is the project's whole defence and it should be stated in those terms. Section 6 is worth flagging as a negative: SRL knew how to write an express carve-out (teachers, search engines) and wrote none for researchers, hobby projects, or games. Section 2 also claims rights in "the selection, coordination, arrangement, and organization" of the Content — a compilation-copyright claim, which is the theory that survives Feist even though the underlying facts do not.
terms.sanctioned_bulk_route: None in this document. Section 5 points onward to two others: the data use and licensing guidelines (data_use.html) and the Bot Traffic/Limiting page (bot-traffic.html) — both fetched and returned as their own rows. The only routes SRL actually offers are (1) paid custom datasets at a $5,000 minimum, (2) the per-table SHARE widget, and (3) a Stathead subscription, which is carved OUT of these Terms entirely: "with the exception of Stathead at www.sports-reference.com/stathead, which is subject to separate terms of use available on that site". There is expressly no API.
terms.enforcement_history: This document is the contractual hook rather than the enforcement record — see the bot-traffic, 429 and blog rows for concrete incidents. Two enforcement-relevant provisions live here: §17, "SRL reserves, in its sole discretion, the right to terminate your access to this Site in the event that you violate any Terms or Conditions of the Agreement or for any reason whatever or no reason, with or without notice"; and §22, "If SRL does take any legal action against you as a result of your violation of the Agreement, SRL will be entitled to recover from you, and you agree to pay, all reasonable attorneys' fees and costs of such action". §20 requires written notice, a 10-business-day exchange, 60 days of negotiation and then mediation before either side litigates — i.e. the contract itself routes a dispute toward a letter and a conversation long before a lawsuit. I found no public record of SRL suing a scraper. Revision history on the page: effective October 1, 2004; updated January 10, 2008; November 1, 2011; January 27, 2015; November 25, 2020; last updated May 19, 2023 — the AI-training clause is a product of one of the two most recent revisions.

terms.document: SR and Data Use ("Acceptable Use of Sports Reference Data")
terms.quote: "In addition to the discussion below, please see our Site Terms of Use specifically clause 5 for permitted uses of our data. We provide an excerpt here for the most relevant part, but you are responsible for understanding the entirety of the Site Terms." | [after excerpting the Terms clauses] "This means that you should not create websites or tools based on data you scrape from Sports Reference or any of our sites or use our data to train generative artificial intelligence models without our permission." | "We have seen an uptick in requests from students, academics and businesses looking to receive custom datasets from our sites, in some cases for free and in some cases for a small fee. These requests occur multiple times a week and sometimes multiple times per day. These requests take a considerable amount of time to negotiate, specify and then produce. Generally we've only been asking for coverage of our time and have attempted to fulfill academic requests on generous terms. However, the rate of requests has forced us to reevaluate this stance." | "There are a couple of additional mitigating factors. For some of our datasets, our licenses completely preclude any redistribution of the data. And, in some cases, we cannot even give you explicit permission to reuse en masse what you find on the site. Additionally, we need to block any aggressive spidering of the site to maintain site performance for non-bot traffic (i.e. actual people using the site)." | "As an aside, copyright law is clear that facts cannot be copyrighted, so you are free to reuse facts found on this site in accordance with copyright laws." | "Moving forward, our data request policy is as follows: We will not fulfill any requests for data for custom downloads, unless you are prepared to pay a minimum of $5,000 for any such request." | "We realize this will be insurmountable for any student requests. However, I would point out that learning how to accumulate data is often a more valuable skill than actually analyzing the data, so we encourage you as a student or professional to learn how. We also realize that your request may not take that long by itself, but when coupled with everyone else's requests it becomes a significant expense for us. There are also many excellent, free data sources listed below. If you are willing to meet our minimum fee, please contact us via our Feedback Form." | "Web Scraping — Please see bot traffic page for information on how we limit and may at times block bot traffic and what our expectations are for responsible bot use." | "Please do not attempt to aggressively spider data from our web sites, as spidering violates the terms and conditions that govern your use of our web sites: Site Terms of Use. If we notice excessive activity from a particular IP address we will be forced to take appropriate measures, which will include, but not be limited to, blocking that IP address. We thank you in advance for respecting our terms of use."
terms.basis: The page is live at the path given — HTTP 200, no redirect, no 404; it is also the page the site footer labels "Acceptable Use of Sports Reference Data" and "Use of Data", so this IS the current canonical location. Whitespace normalized from HTML wrapping; nothing else altered. This page is the single most important document of the four, because it contains the holder's own concession on the point the whole project turns on. (a) CITE ONE FACT: permitted, and here on a much stronger footing than contract language — "copyright law is clear that facts cannot be copyrighted, so you are free to reuse facts found on this site in accordance with copyright laws." That is Sports Reference, in its own voice, on its own site, telling users that reusing facts found there is free. Read it precisely: it is a statement about COPYRIGHT, not a waiver of the contract, and SRL keeps its Terms-of-Use restrictions in the same breath. But it removes any argument that a single sourced fact on a trivia card infringes. (b) EXTRACT FACTS: unclear, and I am marking it unclear rather than restricted because this page contradicts itself within four paragraphs. "You should not create websites or tools based on data you scrape from Sports Reference" is about as direct a prohibition on this project's shape as could be written — and note it reads on the OUTPUT (a website or tool) as much as the method. Yet the same page says you are free to reuse the facts, and "in some cases, we cannot even give you explicit permission to reuse en masse what you find on the site" — an admission that SRL's own licensing prevents it from granting permission it might otherwise grant, which is not the same as forbidding the use. The load-bearing verb is "scrape": every prohibition on this page attaches to automated bulk collection ("scrape", "aggressively spider", "excessive activity from a particular IP address"), while the permission attaches to "facts found on this site". Hand-reading a page and writing a card down is on the permitted side of that line; a crawler that walks a thousand player pages is on the prohibited side. What makes it unclear and not permitted is that "create websites or tools based on data you scrape" reaches the artifact, so the safe reading is that the manner of collection determines the answer and the project must be able to say honestly that it did not scrape. (c) AGGREGATE AT SCALE: prohibited — this page excerpts and adopts the material-substitute clause from Terms §5, and adds "we cannot even give you explicit permission to reuse en masse what you find on the site". "En masse" is their word.
terms.sanctioned_bulk_route: YES — this page names the only sanctioned bulk route SRL operates, and it is priced: "We will not fulfill any requests for data for custom downloads, unless you are prepared to pay a minimum of $5,000 for any such request. ... If you are willing to meet our minimum fee, please contact us via our Feedback Form" (https://www.sports-reference.com/feedback/). That is a real, open door — custom datasets to spec, $5,000 floor, no upper bound stated, negotiated case by case. It is almost certainly the wrong trade for a trivia bank of a few thousand cards, but it means a bulk basketball dataset from the rights holder IS purchasable, which is worth knowing before anyone concludes the data is unobtainable. The page also lists third-party paid providers it will refer you to — Sports Info Solutions, Sports Direct Inc (a Gracenote subsidiary), and Spotrac for contract data ("Please tell them that we forwarded you to them") — and free sources, though the free ones are baseball and hockey only (Lahman Baseball Database, RetroSheet.org, Hockey Summary Project). There is NO free basketball dump and NO API; the API refusal is stated on the linked bot-traffic page. NOTE the licensing wrinkle that limits even the paid route: "For some of our datasets, our licenses completely preclude any redistribution of the data."
terms.enforcement_history: The page states the enforcement mechanism in the first person and without hedging: "If we notice excessive activity from a particular IP address we will be forced to take appropriate measures, which will include, but not be limited to, blocking that IP address." The remedy named is IP blocking, not litigation — consistent with everything else I found. The volume claim is itself evidence of scale: data requests arriving "multiple times a week and sometimes multiple times per day", enough that SRL abandoned a previously generous academic policy and set a $5,000 floor. Undated on its face, but it postdates the Bot Traffic page it links to (October 26, 2022).

Disallow:

Disallow: /dump/

Disallow: /play-index/plus/*.cgi?*

terms.basis: This is the complete file, byte for byte, HTTP 200, fetched today — not an excerpt. Read it against Terms §6, which makes robots.txt contractually operative: "Search engines are expected to follow the guidelines set forth in the robots.txt file that we provide." Four things matter and three of them are easy to miss. FIRST, the named blocks. Three User-agent groups get Disallow: / — a commercial SEO crawler (AhrefsBot), a set of plagiarism-detection bots (SlySearch and friends; the HAL9000/Skynet/The-Matrix entries are a boilerplate joke list, not real agents), and — the one that matters here — GPTBot, OpenAI's crawler, blocked from the entire site. That is the same policy as the AI-training clause in Terms §5, expressed in machine-readable form. It is a statement about crawlers, not about a person reading a page, but the direction of travel is unambiguous: SRL does not want AI systems traversing this site. Twitterbot is the only agent granted an explicit allow ("Disallow:" with an empty value), for link unfurls. SECOND, and this is the finding that changes what is fetchable: the User-agent: * block does NOT disallow /players/, /leagues/, /teams/, /boxscores/, /awards/, /draft/ or /coaches/. Those are the pages the project's ~1,500 citations actually point at, and they are open to any agent. What IS blocked is the deep per-player split data — */gamelog/, */splits/, */on-off/, */lineups/, */shooting/ — precisely the highest-volume, lowest-marginal-value pages, which is a rate-protection choice rather than a secrecy one. Anything sourced from a gamelog or splits URL is on the wrong side of this file even though the parent player page is fine. /play-index/*.cgi?* blocks the old query-builder, the Stathead precursor. THIRD, Crawl-delay: 3 — three seconds between requests, i.e. 20 requests per minute, which matches the numeric limit on the bot-traffic page exactly. Two independent documents agreeing on 20/min is a real ceiling, not a guess. FOURTH, on the three activities: (a) is permitted because robots.txt governs automated retrieval and says nothing about a human reading one page. (b) is restricted rather than permitted — allowed paths only, 3-second delay, and the GPTBot line makes an AI-driven fetcher an awkward fit for the spirit of the file even though no rule names one. (c) is restricted rather than prohibited ON THIS DOCUMENT ALONE, because robots.txt caps rate and scope but does not address purpose; the prohibition on aggregation comes from Terms §5, not from here. Do not read the open /players/ path as permission to bulk-collect — robots.txt is the crawler protocol, and the contract sits above it.
terms.sanctioned_bulk_route: None — robots.txt offers no sitemap dump or bulk endpoint. What it does offer, which is worth more than it looks, is an explicit and generous rate: Crawl-delay: 3. A fetcher that honours 3 seconds, stays on /players/ and /leagues/, and identifies itself honestly is inside every published numeric limit SRL states anywhere. There is no /dump/ available either — it is listed as Disallow.
terms.enforcement_history: The Crawl-delay is enforced in infrastructure, not on trust: exceeding roughly 20 requests/minute returns the 429 page (https://www.sports-reference.com/429.html) and Cloudflare bot filtering has been applied to the basketball site specifically since October 2022 (see the blog row). Concrete downstream evidence that the file's limits bind real projects: the widely used vishaalagartha/basketball_reference_scraper README states "Sports Reference recently instituted a rate limiter preventing users from making an excess of 20 requests/minute. This package abstracts the waiting logic to ensure you never hit this threshold", and links to bot-traffic.html — a third-party scraper library building its architecture around this exact number.

terms.document: Bot/Scraping/Crawler Traffic on Sports-Reference.com Sites (posted October 26, 2022; Update: May 29, 2024)
terms.quote: "Sports Reference is primarily dependent on ad revenue, so we must ensure that actual people using web browsers have the best possible experience when using this site. Unfortunately, non-human traffic, ie bots, crawlers, scrapers, can overwhelm our servers with the number of requests they send us in a short amount of time. Therefore we are implementing rate limiting on the site. We will attempt to keep this page up to date with our current settings." | "Currently we will block users sending requests to: FBref and Stathead sites more often than ten requests in a minute. our other sites more often than twenty requests in a minute. This is regardless of bot type and construction and pages accessed. If you violate this rule your session will be in jail for up to a day." | "Why Not Provide an API? Most of our data comes from third parties who sell the data to us. As part of our agreements with them we can not provide the data available as a download on our site. We are aware that an API would mitigate some issues, but it's not our business model." | "For more information on data use of SR sites, see our Data Use page."
terms.basis: This is the page Terms §5 and data_use.html both point to by name ("our Bot Traffic/Limiting page", "Please see bot traffic page"), which makes it incorporated guidance rather than a stray blog post. Whitespace normalized; the bullet list is quoted in order. It is a RATE document, not a rights document — every verdict here is about how fast, never about whether, so none of the three activities is prohibited by anything on this page and (a) is untouched by it entirely. The operative numbers, which are the most useful concrete thing in this whole sweep: twenty requests per minute on basketball-reference.com (the ten-per-minute tier is FBref and Stathead only), "regardless of bot type and construction and pages accessed" — so there is no user-agent or path you can pick that raises the ceiling — and the penalty is a session ban "for up to a day". That is a published, numeric, unambiguous limit, and it agrees exactly with Crawl-delay: 3 in robots.txt. (b) and (c) are restricted on the twenty-per-minute clause: any extraction or aggregation is lawful-as-to-rate only below that line, and the ceiling makes large-scale collection slow enough to be self-limiting — a thousand pages is fifty minutes of polite fetching at best. Note the honest framing of SRL's motive, which is worth carrying into any conversation with them: the objection stated here is to server load and lost ad revenue, NOT to reuse of the facts. That is a different complaint from the competing-database clause in the Terms, and it is one a low-volume, credit-giving trivia project can answer easily. IMPORTANT CONFLICT, flagged rather than resolved: the 429 error page (returned as its own row) states different numbers — twenty per minute for all sites, jail for one hour, and "You accessed more than thirty pages in less than a minute." This page is the newer of the two (updated May 29, 2024; the 429 page still carries a 2000-2023 copyright line) and says of itself "We will attempt to keep this page up to date with our current settings", so treat bot-traffic.html as governing and the 429 page as stale. Where they differ, the stricter number is the safe one.
terms.sanctioned_bulk_route: NO — and this page is where the door is explicitly closed, in SRL's own words and with a reason: "Why Not Provide an API? Most of our data comes from third parties who sell the data to us. As part of our agreements with them we can not provide the data available as a download on our site. We are aware that an API would mitigate some issues, but it's not our business model." This is decisive and should end any search for a basketball-reference API or dump. The refusal is not reluctance to be talked round — SRL says it is contractually unable, because it licenses the underlying data rather than owning it. That also explains the $5,000 custom-dataset route on data_use.html and its caveat that some datasets "completely preclude any redistribution". Any approach to SRL should therefore ask for permission to CITE and reuse facts, never for a feed.
terms.enforcement_history: The page states the enforcement itself: rate limiting is live and automated, and violating sessions are jailed "for up to a day". Concrete corroboration with dates: (1) the October 7, 2022 SR blog post announcing Cloudflare bot filtering — "we get scraped. A LOT... We've gotten a number of emails around this this week as people who have been scraping us have found themselves blocked" — enabled specifically on the Basketball site among others; (2) the live 429 interstitial at https://www.sports-reference.com/429.html, which exists as a hand-written page rather than a bare HTTP status, i.e. they serve it often enough to be worth designing; (3) third-party scraper libraries architected around the limit — vishaalagartha/basketball_reference_scraper cites the 20/min limiter in its README and links this page, and its Apify port documents built-in 3-second delays and recommends residential proxies; (4) https://github.com/vishaalagartha/basketball_reference_scraper/issues/110, "Getting Status Code 403 On All Requests", opened 2025-08-05 and still open as of today — I could not read the issue body (the session's GitHub proxy is scoped to aselkridge/ball-knowledge and returned "GitHub access to this repository is not enabled for this session" for both the API and the HTML), so I am reporting only the title, date and state as returned by the issue search, not its contents. I found NO cease-and-desist letter, NO lawsuit and NO DMCA action by Sports Reference against any scraper. The consistent pattern across every document and incident is technical blocking, never legal process.

terms.document: Rate Limited Request (429 error) — the served HTTP 429 interstitial
terms.quote: "We apologize, but you have triggered rate limiting by our cloud service provider. This could be for one of many reasons. You accessed more than thirty pages in less than a minute. You have written a bot that accessed too many files too quickly. Multiple people are accessing the site at the same time via your IP address. You are an employee of ESPN. Generally, we block traffic that we think is from a bot for an hour and traffic that we think is a real user for five minutes. See our Bot Traffic page or our SR and Data Use Page. Report an issue with our site or perhaps our twitter account." | "Bot Policy — Sports Reference is primarily dependent on ad revenue, so we must ensure that actual people using web browsers have the best possible experience when using this site. Unfortunately, non-human traffic, ie bots, crawlers, scrapers, can overwhelm our servers with the number of requests they send us in a short amount of time. Therefore we are implementing rate limiting on the site. We will attempt to keep this page up to date with our current settings. Currently we will block users sending requests to: our sites more often than twenty requests in a minute. This is regardless of bot type and construction and pages accessed. If you violate this rule your session will be in jail for an hour."
terms.basis: This is the actual body SRL serves on an HTTP 429, fetched directly at its canonical URL — I did NOT deliberately trip their rate limiter to obtain it, which would have been the one research method this whole exercise exists to avoid. Whitespace normalized. It carries no rights language at all, so it cannot support a permitted/prohibited verdict on its own; the three columns are inherited from the bot-traffic page whose Bot Policy text this page reproduces. Its value is entirely evidentiary and operational. Two things worth having. FIRST, the block DURATIONS, which appear nowhere else: "Generally we block traffic that we think is from a bot for an hour and traffic that we think is a real user for five minutes." So the penalty is tiered by how human you look, and the cheapest insurance against a long ban is behaving like a browser — real user-agent, no parallelism, human-scale gaps. SECOND, a distinct and stricter trigger than the published 20/min: "You accessed more than thirty pages in less than a minute" — thirty pages, not twenty requests, and pages and requests are not the same unit once assets are counted. The page also concedes a false-positive mode that matters for anyone on shared infrastructure: "Multiple people are accessing the site at the same time via your IP address" — a NAT, an office, a VPN or a cloud runner can be jailed for someone else's traffic. ("You are an employee of ESPN" is a joke, but a revealing one about who they think scrapes them.) STALENESS, stated plainly rather than papered over: this page conflicts with bot-traffic.html on both the tier structure (no separate 10/min FBref+Stathead tier here) and the penalty (an hour here, "up to a day" there), and its footer still reads "Copyright © 2000-2023" with an older nav, against "Update: May 29, 2024" on bot-traffic.html. Treat bot-traffic.html as governing and this as the older text; where they disagree, assume the stricter of the two.
terms.sanctioned_bulk_route: None. Repeats the API refusal verbatim from the bot-traffic page: "Most of our data comes from third parties who sell the data to us. As part of our agreements with them we can not provide the data available as a download on our site. We are aware that an API would mitigate some issues, but it's not our business model."
terms.enforcement_history: This page IS enforcement history — it is the artifact of enforcement, a purpose-built interstitial served to blocked clients rather than a bare status code, which tells you the volume of blocking is high enough to justify designing for it. It is also the top web-search result for basketball-reference rate limiting, meaning enough people hit it to make it the canonical public answer. Concrete durations recorded here: one hour for suspected bots, five minutes for suspected humans — versus "up to a day" on the newer bot-traffic page, so the jail term appears to have been LENGTHENED between the 2022/2023 text and the May 2024 update. No legal action referenced anywhere on the page; the only remedy is the temporary block, and the only offered recourse is "Report an issue with our site or perhaps our twitter account."

terms.document: SR Blog — "New Bot Filtering and Content Delivery Network for Sports Reference Sites", posted by sean [Sean Forman], October 7, 2022
terms.quote: "Our devops department finished our move from AWS's Cloudfront Content Delivery Network (CDN) to Cloudflare's CDN this week." | "Cloudflare also includes bot filtering with this offering. It actively searches for badly behaved bots and proactively blocks them from our site. We are now utilizing this feature because we get scraped. A LOT. And if your bot is badly behaved then we don't want you impacting the performance of the site for our other users. We've gotten a number of emails around this this week as people who have been scraping us have found themselves blocked." | "As of today, this filtering will remain in place for our: Soccer/Football, Basketball, Hockey, College sites. We are turning off the active bot filtering on our baseball and pro football sites at this time. We will re-enable bot filtering the week after the end of their respective seasons." | "What is a well-behaved bot? Please see our Data Use page and our Bot Traffic page for guidance. Note that if you are blocked by our servers, the blocks reset after 24 hours, so with some more polite settings on your bot you may be able to try again the next day." | "We can not provide an API (per our data licensing agreements), and you should not view as a data provider (on par with SportRadar or Genius Sports). This is a role that we do not and can not support with company resources."
terms.basis: Whitespace normalized; quoted in the post's own order. The sentence "you should not view as a data provider" is reproduced exactly as published — the missing word ("view US as") is SRL's typo, not a transcription error on my part. This is a blog post, not terms, so it binds nothing; I am returning it because the task asked for statements published anywhere else and because it is the single best evidence of SRL's operating posture, in the founder's own voice. Its three verdicts are inherited from the documents it points at rather than created here. What it adds that no policy page does. FIRST, the enforcement is CLOUDFLARE, not a homegrown counter: "It actively searches for badly behaved bots and proactively blocks them" — meaning the blocking is behavioural and heuristic, applied before any published numeric limit is reached, and evasion techniques (rotating IPs, spoofed agents, residential proxies) are exactly what it is built to catch. SECOND, and this is the line to remember when judging risk: BASKETBALL is named on the always-filtered list, alongside soccer, hockey and the college sites, while baseball and pro football got filtering switched off seasonally. basketball-reference.com is one of the sites SRL protects hardest, all year. THIRD, a block duration that disagrees with both policy pages again — "the blocks reset after 24 hours" here, one hour on the 429 page, "up to a day" on bot-traffic.html. Three documents, three numbers; assume a day. FOURTH, the API refusal is stated with its reason attached and an explicit disclaimer of the role: SRL is not SportRadar or Genius Sports and does not want to be treated as one.
terms.sanctioned_bulk_route: NO, stated more bluntly here than anywhere else: "We can not provide an API (per our data licensing agreements), and you should not view as a data provider (on par with SportRadar or Genius Sports). This is a role that we do not and can not support with company resources." The post names SportRadar and Genius Sports as the places to go for a feed — an implicit referral to commercial sports-data vendors, alongside the explicit referrals on data_use.html (Sports Info Solutions, Sports Direct/Gracenote, Spotrac). The one concession offered is remediation rather than access: "if you are blocked by our servers, the blocks reset after 24 hours, so with some more polite settings on your bot you may be able to try again the next day" — i.e. a block is a correction, not a ban, and politeness restores access.
terms.enforcement_history: THIS IS THE CONCRETE INCIDENT RECORD, dated October 7, 2022, from the holder. A mass blocking event with a stated cause and stated victims: SRL migrated to Cloudflare, switched on active bot filtering, and "We've gotten a number of emails around this this week as people who have been scraping us have found themselves blocked." The admission "we get scraped. A LOT" quantifies the pressure. Timeline of the enforcement regime as reconstructed from the four documents: Oct 7 2022, Cloudflare bot filtering enabled, basketball among the permanently filtered sites, first wave of scrapers blocked; Oct 26 2022, the Bot Traffic page published with the numeric limits; sometime after, the 429 interstitial (copyright line 2000-2023); May 29 2024, Bot Traffic page updated, FBref/Stathead tightened to 10/min and the jail term extended to "up to a day". Downstream evidence of impact on real projects: scraper libraries rebuilt around the limit (vishaalagartha/basketball_reference_scraper README, citing 20/min and linking bot-traffic.html), Apify's port documenting 3-second delays and residential proxies, and an open 403 report at https://github.com/vishaalagartha/basketball_reference_scraper/issues/110 dated 2025-08-05 (title/date/state only — I could not read the body; the session's GitHub access is scoped to aselkridge/ball-knowledge and returned "GitHub access to this repository is not enabled for this session"). Still no cease-and-desist, lawsuit or DMCA notice found anywhere in the public record. SRL's entire demonstrated enforcement toolkit is Cloudflare and a 24-hour timeout.

terms.document: Sharing Information from Sports Reference (the per-table SHARE widget)
terms.quote: "Sports-Reference.com makes it easy to share the data on the site. Via the SHARE link above every table you can now slice and dice any data table on the site and re-use it elsewhere (we just ask you keep the citation to where you got the data)." | "Find the data you want to share. Click on the SHARE link just above the stats next to the header (javascript required). A sharing toolbox appears and buttons to delete columns and rows appear allowing you to pare the data down to just want you want. Please note that any sorting should occur before you delete rows or columns. Next select the output option from html, to iframes, to pre-formatted (good for most internet forums) and more. If we don't have the format you want, let us know via our feedback form." | "You are free to use this data anywhere, we would just ask that you include the citation at the bottom of the table as a courtesy to us for providing this service."
terms.basis: Whitespace normalized; complete body of the page otherwise. This page was not on the assigned list — I found it linked from the footer of every SR page as "How to Share Sports Reference Data" and followed it because the task said a sanctioned route is the most valuable thing available, and this is one. It is a first-party, purpose-built, officially supported mechanism for taking SR data OFF their site and using it elsewhere, and its terms are the most permissive language SRL publishes anywhere: "You are free to use this data anywhere, we would just ask that you include the citation at the bottom of the table as a courtesy." Note the verbs — "we just ask", "as a courtesy" — this is a request, not a condition precedent. (a) and (b) are both permitted on that sentence, with attribution, and (b) is upgraded from restricted (its verdict on the Terms and on data_use.html) to permitted HERE because this route is manual, per-table, human-driven and endorsed: it is extraction by the exact method SRL built for the purpose, so none of the scraping prohibitions attach. It sits squarely inside Terms §5 guiding principle (1) — "sharing, using, modifying, repackaging, or publishing data found on individual SRL webpages is welcomed" — and satisfies principle (2)'s credit requirement by construction, since the citation ships inside the exported markup. (c) remains prohibited: nothing here disturbs the material-substitute clause, and the mechanism is per-table and hand-operated, so it cannot produce a competing store anyway. LIMITS, so this is not over-read: it exports one rendered table at a time, requires JavaScript and a human at the keyboard, and grants nothing about SR's page text, images or logos — only the tabular data. It also does not touch the AI clause in Terms §5, which is about what you then do with the content, not how you obtained it.
terms.sanctioned_bulk_route: YES, and this is the route to actually use — a per-table one rather than a bulk one, but sanctioned, free, unmetered and explicit. Every stats table on basketball-reference.com carries a SHARE link in its header; it opens a toolbox that lets you delete rows and columns down to what you want and export as HTML, iframe, or pre-formatted text, with an SR citation attached at the bottom. SRL's own words for the output: "You are free to use this data anywhere." For a project that cites ~1,500 individual pages and needs discrete facts rather than a mirror, this is a better fit than the $5,000 custom-dataset route on data_use.html, and unlike the API it actually exists. The one thing it demands in exchange — keeping the citation — is something the project already does on every card, which means the workflow is compatible with the holder's preferred method as it stands rather than after a redesign. Practical caveat: JavaScript required, so it is a browser action, not a curl.
terms.enforcement_history: None — and the absence is itself informative. This is the one Sports Reference document with no prohibition, no threat, no rate limit and no reference to blocking in it; the only obligation it states is a citation requested "as a courtesy". Undated on its face and the oldest-feeling page of the set (it still describes the SHARE feature as something you "can now" do), but it is currently linked from the live footer of every SR page and returned HTTP 200 today, so it remains published policy.

terms.basis:
MEASURED, NOT RECALLED: I saved the rendered page to disk and grepped it. The strings 'robot', 'spider', 'scrap', 'crawl' and 'data min' occur ZERO times in the entire Terms of Use. There is no anti-scraping, anti-bot or anti-automation clause. Everything below therefore rests on ownership and use-purpose clauses, not on an access-method clause.

(a) CITE ONE FACT = restricted, on Section 9 clauses (i) and (ii). Not prohibited, but it carries two live conditions the project is not currently meeting: 9(i) requires 'a prominent attribution to NBA.com' on any use, display or publication of NBA Statistics, and 9(ii) limits use to 'legitimate news reporting or private, non-commercial purposes'. A trivia card is neither news reporting nor private. Additionally Section 6 forbids deep links: 'links to internal pages within the Services (e.g., a player page, a photo gallery, or a feature article) ... are not permitted'. The project's house pattern is a link back to the exact page that proves the fact -- that pattern is the one Section 6 names.

(b) EXTRACT FACTS INTO OWN DB = restricted, on Section 1 para 2 and Section 9(ii)/(v). Section 1 permits download 'to any single computer only for your personal, noncommercial use' and forbids distributing or reproducing 'any materials of the Services for public or commercial purposes on any other Website'. Section 9(v) adds that NBA Statistics 'may not be used in connection with any fantasy game or other commercial product or service'. Ball Knowledge is a game; if it is ever commercial, 9(v) reads as a flat prohibition rather than a restriction, and I would move this cell to prohibited. As a private non-commercial build it stays restricted-with-attribution.

(c) AGGREGATE AT SCALE = prohibited, on Section 9(vii) alone, which is written for exactly this activity: NBA Statistics 'may not be used in connection with any website, product, or service that features a database (in any medium or format) of comprehensive, regularly updated statistics from NBA, WNBA or G-League games ... without the Operator's express prior consent.' Note the scope limiters that make this narrower than it first reads: it bites on a database that is BOTH 'comprehensive' AND 'regularly updated'. A finite, hand-curated question bank of historical facts is arguably neither.

SCOPE LIMIT, stated so this is not over-read: Section 9 governs 'NBA Statistics' defined as statistics the Operator 'may make available through the Services'. It is a contract term about stats obtained FROM nba.com. It is not a property claim over the underlying facts, and it does not reach the same numbers sourced from a book, a newspaper archive, or a third-party site with its own terms.

WHAT IS MINE, NOT THE DOCUMENT'S: the verdicts, the commercial/non-commercial branch, and the observation about Section 6 colliding with the project's citation pattern.
terms.sanctioned_bulk_route:
TWO ROUTES EXIST, and both are gates rather than doors.

1. A CONSENT PATH IS WRITTEN INTO THE PROHIBITION. Section 9(vii) ends 'without the Operator's express prior consent', and Section 1 twice says 'without the written permission of the Operator'. The aggregation bar is not absolute -- it is a permission gate, and the NBA has published the standing for asking. This is worth more than it looks: a written request is a cheap move that converts a prohibited cell into a licensed one.

2. developerportal.nba.com EXISTS BUT IS CLOSED. https://developerportal.nba.com/ -- 'Use our APIs to automate, innovate, and gain access to the data that powers the NBA' -- and, verbatim: 'The NBA Developer Portal is only available for NBA Teams and Official NBA Business Partners, please do not reach out without the proper affiliation.' It also states 'No payment is required to sign up, generate API credentials, and use the APIs' -- so it is free but affiliation-gated, not price-gated. Footer reads '(c) 2023 NBA Media Ventures, LLC.' This is a dead end for an independent project, and the page explicitly asks unaffiliated parties not to contact it.

3. THE COMMERCIAL ROUTE IS SPORTRADAR, the NBA's official data distributor (https://developer.sportradar.com/basketball/reference/nba-overview; partnership announced at https://www.nba.com/news/nba-sportradar-genius-sports-partnership-official-release). HONEST LIMIT: I did not fetch or read Sportradar's terms or pricing in this pass, so I am naming the route, not characterising its terms. A search result described entry pricing as 'low thousands per month' -- I am NOT asserting that as fact, I did not verify it against Sportradar's own page.

NO FREE PUBLIC BULK DUMP OR DATA DOWNLOAD WAS FOUND anywhere on nba.com.
terms.enforcement_history: I did not search case law in this pass, and I am not asserting there is or is not NBA litigation over stats scraping -- I have not checked. The concrete enforcement record I did gather is technical, and it lives in the stats.nba.com row below. The one thing worth carrying here: the leading unofficial client, swar/nba_api, points its own users at this exact document. Its README states verbatim: 'NBA.com has a Terms of Use regarding the use of the NBA's digital platforms.' The library does not claim a licence; it hands the reader the ToU.

terms.basis:
WHAT THIS DOCUMENT IS: a crawl-permission file. It governs which automated agents may FETCH which paths. It says nothing about what may be done with what is fetched -- that is the ToU's job. Keeping those apart matters here because the two layers give different answers.

THE FINDING THAT MATTERS MOST TO THIS PROJECT, and it is unambiguous: 'User-agent: anthropic-ai / Disallow: /', 'User-agent: ClaudeBot / Disallow: /', and 'User-agent: Claude-Web / Disallow: /'. All three Anthropic agents are barred from the ENTIRE site with no Allow exceptions -- unlike GPTBot and Google-Extended, which get a carve-out list including /players, /player/*profile$, /team/*, /standings, /schedule, /stats/history and /stats/draft/history. The NBA drew a line and Anthropic crawlers are on the wrong side of it. Any pipeline in this project that fetches nba.com under an Anthropic-identified agent is doing something the site has explicitly refused. DISCLOSURE: I fetched this file and the ToU today under a spoofed Chrome UA string via curl. robots.txt itself is conventionally always fetchable, but the ToU fetch is exactly the thing these three lines disallow. Recording that plainly rather than burying it.

(a) CITE ONE FACT = permitted. No clause in robots.txt speaks to citation, quotation or attribution; it is out of scope for the document. A human opening a page and reading a number is not a crawler.

(b) EXTRACT FACTS = restricted, on the 'User-Agent: *' group. A generic, non-AI-identified crawler is DISALLOWED from only nine path patterns plus the per-team /node/ and /users/ directories. Everything else -- /players, /player/*, /team/*, /stats/* except /stats/events/ -- is crawlable under '*'. But two disallows bite hard on the practical route: 'Disallow: /api/*' blocks the JSON that backs the front end, and 'Disallow: /stats/events/'. And for THIS project the '*' group is irrelevant, because the named-agent groups above override it for Anthropic clients.

(c) AGGREGATE AT SCALE = restricted, same clauses. Note what is ABSENT and would matter for bulk work: there is NO 'Crawl-delay' directive anywhere in the file, for any user-agent. robots.txt sets no rate limit. Anyone treating that silence as permission to hammer the host should read the enforcement column instead.

MINE, NOT THE DOCUMENT'S: the observation that the file contradicts itself on GPTBot and Google-Extended (each appears in two groups, one permissive, one blanket-deny). Under RFC 9309 a crawler must merge groups matching its name, and the merged result for those two is ambiguous. It does not affect Anthropic agents, whose only groups are unqualified denials.
terms.sanctioned_bulk_route: None in this document. There is no dump, no data download, no API tier named here. The only affirmative signal is 'Sitemap: https://www.nba.com/sitemap_index.xml', which advertises the site's URL inventory to crawlers -- useful for enumeration, but it is a map, not a licence, and it does not widen the Anthropic-agent denial one inch.
terms.enforcement_history: How the named-agent denials are enforced in practice is UNKNOWN to me -- I did not test whether nba.com serves or blocks a request presenting a ClaudeBot UA string, and I am not going to guess. Two adjacent facts I did establish: this file returned HTTP 200 to a spoofed Chrome UA from this host, and https://www.nba.com/stats returned HTTP 200 at 447,702 bytes to the same client. So the HTML site is not IP-blocking this address. Whatever blocking exists on the stats API (next rows) is not happening at the level of the web front end.

terms.basis:
ALL THREE CELLS ARE 'unclear' BECAUSE THERE IS NO CLAUSE. A verdict with no clause under it is an opinion, and the instruction says those get discarded -- so I am not manufacturing one from an absent file.

What I can say without inventing text, kept clearly separate as MY reading: under RFC 9309, an absent or 404 robots.txt means a crawler may treat the host as having no robots restrictions. On that reading the robots LAYER imposes nothing on stats.nba.com, and the entire restriction burden shifts to the nba.com Terms of Use -- which do reach this host, because stats.nba.com redirects into www.nba.com/stats and is therefore part of 'nba.com' as the ToU preamble defines the Services.

DO NOT READ THIS ROW AS A GREEN LIGHT. The absence of a robots file on this host is almost certainly an artefact of the 2020-era migration of stats.nba.com onto www.nba.com/stats, not a deliberate grant. And the practical position on this host is the opposite of permissive: as the next row records, the JSON endpoints under stats.nba.com/stats/ do not redirect and do not answer this client at all. A missing robots.txt on a host that silently drops your packets is not permission.

ONE ASYMMETRY WORTH FLAGGING, measured today: the HTML site at stats.nba.com returns 200 and redirects to www.nba.com/stats, where www.nba.com/robots.txt DOES apply -- including the blanket 'User-agent: ClaudeBot / Disallow: /'. So the browsable stats pages are covered by the parent robots file even though the host itself has none. The API paths are the part that falls outside any robots file.
terms.sanctioned_bulk_route: None. A host with no robots.txt publishes no sitemap, no dump, no crawl guidance and no rate guidance. Nothing here to use.
terms.enforcement_history: See the endpoints row. The relevant record for this host is entirely about the API paths, not the robots layer.

By using such NBA Statistics, you agree that: (i) any use, display, or publication of the NBA Statistics shall include a prominent attribution to NBA.com ...; (ii) the NBA Statistics may only be used, displayed, or published for legitimate news reporting or private, non-commercial purposes; ... [1. OWNERSHIP AND USE RESTRICTIONS] "No Basketball Content from the Services may be reproduced, republished, uploaded, posted, modified, reused, transmitted, reproduced, distributed, copied, publicly displayed, linked to, or otherwise used except as provided in these Terms of Use without the written permission of the Operator."

[14. TERMINATION OF SERVICE] "The Operator may change, suspend, or discontinue any aspect of the Services at any time, including, but not limited to, the availability of any Services feature, database, or content. The Operator may also impose limits on certain features and services or restrict your access to parts or the entirety of the Services without notice or liability at any time in the Operator’s exclusive discretion, without prejudice to any legal or equitable remedies available to the Operator, for any reason or purpose ..."
terms.basis:
THE HEADLINE, SAID PLAINLY: THERE IS NO DOCUMENT. The stats.nba.com/stats/* endpoints are undocumented, unversioned and unannounced. The NBA publishes no API terms of service, no developer agreement, no acceptable-use policy and no rate limit for them. Anyone who tells you otherwise is quoting a blog post. This means there is no clause granting access, and equally no clause specifically forbidding it -- the endpoints are simply unaddressed. That silence is not a licence; it is an absence of one.

WHICH CLAUSE REACHES AN API, since that was the question: the ToU preamble defines the Services to include 'League websites (including, but not limited to nba.com ...)' and 'online content offerings'. stats.nba.com 301s into www.nba.com/stats (verified today, Location header quoted in the row above), so it is part of nba.com by the NBA's own routing. 'Online content offerings' is the phrase doing the work for a JSON endpoint that is not a website page. Section 9 then attaches independently of transport: it governs 'NBA Statistics' the Operator 'may make available through the Services', which is what these endpoints return, whether reached by browser or by script.

(a) CITE ONE FACT = restricted, on 9(i) attribution and 9(ii) news-reporting-or-private-non-commercial.
(b) EXTRACT FACTS = restricted, on 9(ii) and Section 1's 'personal, noncommercial use' limit; flips to PROHIBITED under 9(v) if the product is commercial.
(c) AGGREGATE AT SCALE = prohibited, on 9(vii) verbatim -- the 'comprehensive, regularly updated statistics' database clause. Scraping these endpoints in bulk to build a stats database is the precise fact pattern 9(vii) describes.

A POINT THAT IS EASY TO GET WRONG AND MATTERS: no API terms means no CONTRACTUAL rate limit -- but Section 14 reserves the right to 'impose limits ... or restrict your access to parts or the entirety of the Services without notice or liability at any time in the Operator's exclusive discretion'. The NBA has pre-authorised itself to do exactly the blocking documented below, and to do it silently. A timeout is not a bug report; it is the reserved remedy being exercised.

MINE, NOT THE DOCUMENT'S: every verdict above, the 'online content offerings' reading, and the judgement that silence is not permission.
terms.sanctioned_bulk_route: NONE for these endpoints, and this is the most consequential negative finding in the set. There is no official tier, no key, no quota, no paid plan for stats.nba.com. The three routes that do exist are covered in the Terms of Use row: (1) written consent under 9(vii)/Section 1, (2) developerportal.nba.com, closed to all but 'NBA Teams and Official NBA Business Partners', (3) Sportradar as official commercial distributor, terms unread by me. For an independent project, the honest summary is that the undocumented endpoints are the ONLY free bulk route, and they are the unsanctioned one. HONEST NOTE ON A NEARBY HOST: cdn.nba.com (which backs nba_api's 'live' module) returned HTTP 403 AccessDenied on /robots.txt today -- an S3-style error, so it is a bucket with no robots file rather than a governed API. It publishes no terms either.
terms.enforcement_history:
KEEPING TWO THINGS APART: what follows is evidence of what the NBA's servers DO. It is not evidence of what the terms SAY, and community bug reports are not legal authority. Read it as an operational record.

FIRST-HAND, TODAY (2026-08-07, this machine): two requests to stats.nba.com/stats/* hung to full timeout, zero bytes, no HTTP status -- once bare, once with the complete canonical browser header set including x-nba-stats-origin: stats and x-nba-stats-token: true, Referer and Origin https://www.nba.com. The control request to stats.nba.com/ succeeded at 200 / 447,702 bytes from the same IP in the same minute. HOW FAR THAT GOES: a silent drop on the API path with a 200 on the HTML path is consistent with datacenter-IP filtering targeted at the API. I CANNOT prove intent from a timeout, and I am not claiming to -- I am reporting the measurement.

THE PUBLIC RECORD, dated, from swar/nba_api issues (github.com/swar/nba_api/issues/N). This is an eight-year unbroken chain, which is the point -- it is not one outage:
#5 'JSONDecodeError when hitting endpoints' 2018-10-01 | #12 'Requests/sec' 2018-10-10 | #69 'Any idea what a reasonable request rate is?' 2019-04-26 | #100 'ConnectionResetError: [WinError 10054]' 2019-11-15 | #106 'stats endpoints not working?' 2019-11-24 | #124 'API not working? Timeout' 2020-01-23, 54 comments | #153 'Most endpoints not working' 2020-05-20 | #155 'Is the API still working? Are there new headers?' 2020-07-20 | #168 'No API Calls Working' 2020-09-08 | #175 2020-11-02 | #176 'HTTPSConnectionPool(host=\'stats.nba.com\', port=443): Read timed out. (read timeout=30)' 2020-11-03, 27 comments | #199 2021-01-13 | #273 'Getting timeouts locally on shotchartdetail endpoint' 2022-10-08 | #320 'NBA API: timeout for /stats endpoints' 2022-12-28, STILL OPEN | #389 '[Bug]: API endpoints all timeout in browser or using curl' 2023-10-22 | #572 'leaguegamefinder request timing out on first request' 2025-10-20 | #621 'Noticed issues calling boxscoreadvanced and traditional V2 & V3' 2025-12-25 | #633 'Issue with multiple requests' 2026-02-19, 27 comments, OPEN | #650 'Reccomended rate limit' 2026-03-05, OPEN | #678 'nba_api.live silently swallows 403s and raises a misleading JSONDecodeError' 2026-05-27, OPEN.

VERBATIM FROM THAT RECORD:
- #650 body, in full: 'Title. I want to know how long I should wait between requests to avoid IP bans.' Opened 2026-03-05, still unanswered five months later. Nobody knows the rate limit, because nobody publishes one.
- #633, reporter christophermlight, on hitting ReadTimeoutError on the SECOND request in a script: 'Does this have something to do with the way that nba_api manages requests and the way NBA.com limits them?'
- #389, opened 2023-10-22: 'All of the endpoints here time out' / 'is the nba api toast now?'

THE PATTERN THE RECORD SHOWS: failures are TIMEOUTS AND SILENT DROPS, not 403s with an explanatory body. #678's title is the tell -- a 403 arrives disguised, and the client mistakes it for malformed JSON. There is no error message telling you that you have been blocked, which is why the same issue gets reopened every few months by someone who thinks the service is down.

CLOUD IP RANGES ARE BLOCKED WHOLESALE. Reported at https://medium.com/@inman.justin/working-around-nba-coms-ip-ban-for-cloud-hosted-nba-api-apps, titled 'Working Around NBA.com's IP Ban for Cloud-Hosted NBA-API Apps'; the community-reported workaround is routing through a VPS on a residential-ish range. CAVEAT I AM NOT GLOSSING: that is a Medium post, not primary evidence, and I did not verify its claims beyond noting my own timeouts are consistent with them.

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR PLANNING, mine not theirs: any Ball Knowledge pipeline that depends on stats.nba.com from CI, a cloud runner, or this sandbox should be assumed BROKEN BY DEFAULT, not intermittently flaky. Budget for it failing rather than for retrying it.

terms.basis:
All three are 'unclear' because the governing terms sit behind a login this project cannot pass, and I will not characterise a document I could not read. What the PUBLIC page establishes is eligibility, not permissions: 'The NBA Developer Portal is only available for NBA Teams and Official NBA Business Partners, please do not reach out without the proper affiliation.' That single sentence closes the route for an independent project, and it also asks unaffiliated parties not to make contact -- so 'just email them and ask' is specifically declined here, and any consent request should instead go through the Section 9(vii) / Section 1 written-permission path in the Terms of Use.

THE ONE GENUINELY USEFUL FACT: 'No payment is required to sign up, generate API credentials, and use the APIs.' The official NBA API is FREE. The barrier is affiliation, not money. That reframes the problem -- there is no amount of budget that buys this particular door, which is why the commercial route is Sportradar rather than the NBA directly.

MINE, NOT THE DOCUMENT'S: everything after the two quoted sentences.
terms.sanctioned_bulk_route: THIS IS THE SANCTIONED ROUTE, and it is closed to us. https://developerportal.nba.com/ -- official, free, credentialed, and restricted to 'NBA Teams and Official NBA Business Partners'. Recording it so no future session spends time rediscovering it and concluding it might be worth applying to. It is not. The realistic options remain: (1) a written consent request to the Operator under ToU Section 9(vii)'s 'express prior consent' and Section 1's 'written permission' language, (2) a paid Sportradar licence as official distributor, or (3) sourcing facts from holders other than the NBA entirely -- which, given Section 9 only governs stats obtained FROM the Services, is the cleanest way out of this whole clause.
terms.enforcement_history: None to report -- an affiliation gate is enforced by the login, not by after-the-fact action. Nothing found about the NBA acting against anyone for attempting to register.

terms.basis: ANSWERING THE REDIRECT QUESTION FIRST, BECAUSE IT WAS ASKED EXPLICITLY: https://www.wnba.com/terms-of-use does NOT redirect. curl -w url_effective returned final_url=https://www.wnba.com/terms-of-use, http=200, Terms of Use - WNBA, canonical=/terms-of-use. The WNBA publishes its own Terms of Use as a distinct document, with WNBA Enterprises, LLC (not NBA Media Ventures) named as the "Operator". BUT the answer has a second half that matters more than the first: the substantive content is the NBA's document with the nouns swapped. The statistics section is still literally headed "NBA STATISTICS", still defines its subject as "NBA Statistics", and still sweeps in "WNBA, National Basketball Association, G League, 2K League, and Basketball Africa League" in one definition. Practically: the WNBA publishes its own terms, and those terms say the same thing as the NBA's. Treating a WNBA fact as governed by NBA-family rules is correct in substance and wrong in citation — cite THIS document, not nba.com/termsofuse. (a) CITE ONE PAGE TO PROVE ONE FACT, WITH A LINK BACK = RESTRICTED, and the LINK-BACK HALF IS THE PART THAT FAILS. Two separate clauses bite in opposite directions. The fact-citation half is permitted under conditions: § NBA STATISTICS (i) "any use, display, or publication of the NBA Statistics shall include a prominent attribution to WNBA.com" — so attribution is not optional courtesy, it is the licence condition, and "prominent" is the adjective. But (ii) confines that permitted use to "legitimate news reporting or private, non-commercial purposes". The link-back half is worse: § LINKS states flatly that "All links to Services from a Permissible Site must be to the Services’ home page or to the homepage of a particular team — links to internal pages within the Services (e.g., a player page, a photo gallery, or a feature article) other than to the home page of a League’s team are not permitted." A per-card citation link pointing at a specific player page or stats table is exactly the enumerated example of a prohibited link. The permitted link is to wnba.com itself or to a team homepage, as a word link, not a logo. So the honest verdict on (a) is: the citation is restricted (attribution + non-commercial/news), and the deep link that makes the citation checkable is affirmatively not permitted. (b) EXTRACT INDIVIDUAL FACTS INTO OWN DATABASE, THEN CITE = PROHIBITED for this project, on clause (ii) before you even reach commerciality. § NBA STATISTICS (ii): "the NBA Statistics may only be used, displayed, or published for legitimate news reporting or private, non-commercial purposes." A published, publicly playable game is neither news reporting nor private — it fails the test on "private" regardless of whether money changes hands, so the DESIGN.md §11 "credits, never real money" guardrail does not rescue it here. Clause (v) then closes the second door independently: "the NBA Statistics may not be used in connection with any fantasy game or other commercial product or service." Ball Knowledge is not a fantasy game, but "or other commercial product or service" reaches any monetised version. And § OWNERSHIP AND USE RESTRICTIONS independently limits downloads to "any single computer only for your personal, noncommercial use" and bars "distribute, reproduce, republish, upload, display, modify, transmit, reuse, repost, link to, or use any materials of the Services for public or commercial purposes on any other websites or otherwise without the written permission of the Operator". Note "link to" appears inside that prohibition list — the WNBA has drafted linking itself as an act of use. The narrow carve-out that does exist: private research use, and genuine news reporting with prominent WNBA.com attribution. (c) AGGREGATE AT SCALE = PROHIBITED, on the single most explicit clause in the document. § NBA STATISTICS (vii): "the NBA Statistics may not be used in connection with any website, product, or service that features a database (in any medium or format) of comprehensive, regularly updated statistics from League, NBA, G-League, 2K League, or Basketball Africa League games, competitions, or events without the Operator’s express prior consent." Three drafted-tight phrases to note: "in any medium or format" defeats any argument that a JSON file or a game's internal bank is not a database; "in connection with" reaches a product that merely uses such a database, not only one that publishes it; and "without the Operator’s express prior consent" means the gate is a permission you must go and ask for, not a condition you can satisfy yourself. Clause (vi) adds a separate bar on "real-time or archived play-by-play account or depiction of any League game" — relevant if the project ever ingests play-by-play. § INJUNCTIVE RELIEF is the stated remedy and is pre-agreed: the user consents in advance that violations "may result in irreparable injury" and that the League "may obtain injunctions". WHAT THIS IS AND IS NOT (my analysis, not the document): this is a contract of adhesion governing access to their Services, not a copyright claim over the underlying facts. Under US law a game score or a career rebound total is an uncopyrightable fact, and a fact learned from wnba.com and then verified against an independent source is not obviously governed by a contract about wnba.com. The clean, cheap route for this project is therefore: do not source WNBA facts FROM wnba.com/stats.wnba.com at all. Take them from Basketball-Reference, Wikipedia, or contemporaneous news reporting, and cite those. That sidesteps clauses (ii), (v), (vii) and the deep-link ban in one move, at no cost to accuracy. Where wnba.com is genuinely the only source, the compliant posture is: prominent "WNBA.com" attribution on the card, a word link to wnba.com's home page rather than a deep link, and no bulk pull. ONE THING I COULD NOT CHECK AND AM NOT GUESSING AT: https://www.wnba.com/robots.txt returned HTTP 403 with an S3 AccessDenied body, so the wnba.com crawl policy is unreadable. I did not substitute a remembered version. (stats.wnba.com's robots.txt IS readable — see the second row, and it is surprising.) Also verified by grep: the words "spider", "scrape", "robot" and "harvest" appear ZERO times in this document — there is no anti-scraping or anti-automation clause at all. The restrictions here are all about USE and REPUBLICATION, not about the act of retrieval. That is a meaningful asymmetry and it means the operative risk is what you SHIP, not how you FETCH.
terms.sanctioned_bulk_route: NONE FOUND, and I looked. There is no data download, no dump, no documented API tier, and no developer portal linked from this document or from the WNBA footer. The full footer link list rendered on the terms page is: General Information, Newsletter Sign Up, Career Opportunities, Contact the WNBA, Officiating Information, Gaming Operators, License Application, Help Center, About the WNBA, Changemakers, League History, Key Dates, Rules of the Game, Fan Code of Conduct, FAQ, More NBA Sites (NBA / NBA 2K / Junior NBA / G League / Basketball Africa League), Privacy Policy, California/Colorado/EEA-UK/Brazil Privacy Statements, Customer Support, Terms of Use, League Pass Terms of Use, Accessibility and Closed Captions, Cookie Policy, Do Not Sell My Personal Information. Nothing resembling data licensing or a developer programme. THE ONLY DOOR THE DOCUMENT ITSELF OPENS is a permission request: clause (vii) bars database use "without the Operator’s express prior consent", and § OWNERSHIP repeatedly conditions on "the written permission of the Operator" — i.e. the sanctioned route is to write to WNBA Enterprises, LLC and ask. That is the same shape as the BLACKFIVES-OUTREACH.md pending action already in this repo. Two adjacent items worth noting rather than overstating: (1) the footer carries "Gaming Operators" and "License Application" links, which are a sports-betting licensing path, not a stats-data path — I did not fetch them and do not claim they license data; (2) I attempted the undocumented stats.wnba.com JSON endpoint family (GET /stats/alltimeleadersgrids?LeagueID=10...) and the request TIMED OUT after 25s with zero bytes, so I cannot even confirm it responds, let alone call it sanctioned. It is not documented, not linked, and not covered by any permissive term — do not treat it as a route.
terms.enforcement_history: NOT ESTABLISHED FROM ANY DOCUMENT I FETCHED, and I am not filling this from memory. I read the Terms of Use and the stats site; neither contains an enforcement record, and I did not retrieve any litigation docket, cease-and-desist, or news report today. What I CAN report is only what the document says about its own remedies, which is not the same thing as history: § INJUNCTIVE RELIEF secures advance consent to injunctive relief and waives the bond requirement; § TERMINATION OF SERVICE reserves the right to "restrict your access to parts or the entirety of the Services without notice or liability at any time in the Operator’s exclusive discretion" and requires that on termination "you shall immediately discontinue your use of and access to the Services and destroy all materials obtained from them"; § DISPUTE RESOLUTION imposes binding arbitration under NAM rules with a class-action and jury-trial waiver. Treat the arbitration clause as the practical enforcement channel for an individual developer. If Aaron wants real enforcement history, that is a separate targeted search and should be run as one.

terms.basis:
WHAT THIS ROW ADDS: the brief asked whether a WNBA statistics or historical-records page carries its OWN usage language. It does not. stats.wnba.com is a separate host from www.wnba.com, it is where wnba.com/stats and the all-time-leaders records pages actually land, and it publishes no terms, no attribution notice, and no copyright footer in its served HTML. The absence is itself the finding, and it is a documented absence rather than a failure to look — see the four probes quoted above.

WHAT GOVERNS IT, THEN: the WNBA.com Terms of Use, by that document's own definition of scope and by nothing else. The preamble quoted in the first row extends the terms to "the digital platforms of the Women’s National Basketball Association ... including League websites (including, but not limited to wnba.com), apps ... and online content offerings (collectively, the “Services”)." The phrase "including, but not limited to wnba.com" is what reaches this host. I want to be precise about the weakness there, because it cuts both ways: I could NOT find a served link from stats.wnba.com back to the wnba.com Terms of Use (the footer bundle carries an example.com placeholder), so the binding is by the ToU's definition of "Services", not by any notice a visitor to stats.wnba.com actually sees. The verdicts for (a), (b) and (c) are therefore identical to the first row and rest on the identical clauses — § NBA STATISTICS (i)/(ii) for citing, (ii)/(v) for extraction, (vii) for aggregation — because there is no second document to change them.

THE ROBOTS.TXT IS GENUINELY SURPRISING AND SHOULD NOT BE MISREAD. The complete file is two lines: a Sitemap directive and a bare "User-agent: *" with NO Disallow directive following it. Under RFC 9309 a group with no Disallow rule imposes no crawl restriction, so at the robots layer this host permits crawling of everything, and the sitemap actively hands crawlers indexes of every player page and every team page. Combined with the first row's grep result — the words "spider", "scrape", "robot" and "harvest" appear zero times in the Terms of Use — the WNBA has, unusually, no technical or contractual restriction on the ACT OF FETCHING at all. THE TRAP: that is not a licence and must not be reported to Aaron as one. robots.txt governs crawler etiquette; the Terms of Use govern what you may DO with what you fetched, and clauses (ii), (v) and (vii) are unaffected by a permissive robots file. The correct summary is: fetching is unrestricted, USE is heavily restricted, and it is use that this project needs. Do not let an open robots.txt talk the project into a bulk pull that clause (vii) then prohibits.

CONTRAST WORTH RECORDING: https://www.wnba.com/robots.txt returned HTTP 403 AccessDenied (an S3 error body, i.e. misconfiguration rather than deliberate blocking), while https://stats.wnba.com/robots.txt returns 200. The two WNBA hosts are administered differently, and the stats host is the one that is readable.

PRACTICAL BEARING ON BALL KNOWLEDGE: stats.wnba.com is the natural place to go for WNBA all-time leaders and franchise records, and it will not stop you. The recommendation from the first row stands unchanged and is if anything sharper here — prove WNBA card facts against Basketball-Reference or contemporaneous reporting and cite those, because a fact taken from stats.wnba.com carries clause (ii) ("private, non-commercial purposes"), clause (i) (mandatory prominent WNBA.com attribution) and the deep-link ban into the card, and a fact taken from Basketball-Reference does not.
terms.sanctioned_bulk_route: NONE. No download, no export, no documented API, no developer page, and no terms page of any kind on this host — /terms, /terms-of-use and /legal all resolve to https://stats.wnba.com/error/. The nearest thing to a bulk affordance is the sitemap index quoted above (sitemap_base.xml, sitemap_players.xml, sitemap_teams.xml, all lastmod 2026-06-29), which enumerates the site's player and team URLs and is explicitly advertised to crawlers by robots.txt. THAT IS A DISCOVERY AID, NOT A DATA LICENCE, and I am flagging it as such rather than dressing it up: it tells you which pages exist, it does not grant any right to build a database from them, and clause (vii) of the WNBA Terms of Use prohibits exactly that use without express prior consent. I also probed the undocumented stats.wnba.com JSON endpoint family used by the site's own front end and the request timed out with zero bytes returned, so I make no claim about it whatsoever — it is undocumented, unlinked, and unsanctioned. The only real route to bulk WNBA data remains a written permission request to WNBA Enterprises, LLC.
terms.enforcement_history: NONE FETCHED, NONE ASSERTED. This host publishes no enforcement notice, no rate-limit policy, no usage warning and no terms, so there is nothing on it to quote. I did not retrieve any external enforcement record today and will not reconstruct one from memory. The only enforcement language anywhere in the WNBA's published stack is in the Terms of Use itself (§ INJUNCTIVE RELIEF, § TERMINATION OF SERVICE, § DISPUTE RESOLUTION), quoted in the first row — and those are stated remedies, not evidence that any of them has ever been used against a fan project.

7. Licensing of Content

GNU Free Documentation License ("GFDL") (unversioned, with no invariant sections, front-cover texts, or back-cover texts).

The only exception is if the Project edition or feature requires a different license. In that case, you agree to license any text you contribute under the particular license prescribed by the Project edition or the feature.

Please note that these licenses do allow commercial uses of your contributions, as long as such uses are compliant with the terms of the respective licenses.
